correctness.rationale: For all positive balanced finite target vectors, the capped stationarity equations give two strictly increasing demand caps C,D. Their inverse-product function Psi(R) is strictly increasing on 0<R<T with range (0,K_c), proving existence/uniqueness below threshold. At full target, stationarity is a feasible one-parameter segment that exists iff K>=K_c. The exact top-level multiplicity formula gives the one-sided deficit slope; Jacobian quotient and within-side differences give the neutral and stable eigenvalues; symmetry reduces homogeneous flow to a projected two-dimensional system and proves initial-imbalance clipping. value.rationale: Balanced aggregate target rates are the explicit boundary excluded from the motivating paper. The theorem settles its complete equilibrium multiplicity transition for arbitrary heterogeneity, quantitatively identifies how unmet demand disappears at that sharp critical encounter rate, and supplies an exact initial-condition selection law that explains the resulting lack of unique prediction. These are structural and interpretation-relevant facts about matching-rate adaptation, not a finite table or cosmetic special case.
